S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by a combination of positive symptoms (such as hallucinations and delusions), disorganized thinking and behavior, and negative symptoms (such as diminished emotional expression, reduced motivation, and social withdrawal) that lead to marked functional impairment. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence or early adulthood, but late-onset cases can occur, especially in women and in the context of medical comorbidities or psychosocial stressors. The course is often chronic with episodic exacerbations, and negative symptoms and cognitive deficits tend to be most strongly associated with long-term disability. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the prominence and persistence of psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes, and from brief or schizophreniform psychoses by its longer duration and functional decline.

patient.personality: Marie is an outgoing, talkative caregiver who thrives on lively social interactions, spontaneous community involvement, and bringing warmth and creativity into everyday routines.
patient.stressor: About three and a half years ago, Marie and her husband went through a prolonged period of marital strain related to financial pressures, disagreements about having another child, and his frequent work-related travel, which left her feeling increasingly unsupported at home. At the same time, conflicts with a demanding parent at the daycare and a tense investigation after an unfounded complaint left her worrying constantly about being blamed or misunderstood, undermining the confidence she once had in her caretaking role. Over the following months, her friends and coworkers noticed a dramatic shift: she stopped organizing potlucks, declined invitations to festivals and concerts, and began sitting quietly during breaks instead of chatting and joking, often staring off and letting classroom preparation tasks slide. As this pattern of emotional blunting, loss of initiative, and social withdrawal deepened and persisted over more than two years—impacting her performance at work, her marriage, and her community involvement—her supervisor, together with her husband, urged her to seek psychiatric help when she began talking about possibly quitting her job because she “just couldn’t bring herself to care anymore.”
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve lost my spark—I don’t feel like talking, going out, or putting effort into anything the way I used to.”

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: A lot of days at the daycare and even at home, I hear this man’s voice right behind me, clear as if he’s in the room, saying things like, “They’re watching you,” or repeating what I just thought, and when I turn around there’s never anyone there, but it still feels completely real and makes it hard to focus on the kids or even follow what my husband is saying.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: Sometimes in the middle of class or even during a staff meeting, I’ll just freeze standing in one spot or sit there staring at a wall, holding the same toy or piece of paper for ages, barely moving even when someone calls my name or asks me to help, like my body and brain won’t cooperate and I can’t get myself to respond the way I know I’m supposed to.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: I used to be the one planning crafts, joking with the kids and chatting with the other teachers, but now most days I just sit there feeling flat and tired, answering people with a few words if I have to, letting the dishes and lesson plans pile up because I can’t seem to care enough to start anything or enjoy the things I used to look forward to, like girls’ nights or family outings.
